items.name: Trolley jack
items.why: Lifts at the body crossmember at the front and the rear subframe, on a wood block.

items.name: Axle stands, pair or two pairs
items.why: Carry the car at the four sill jacking points.

items.name: Wheel chocks
items.why: Jaguar says not to trust the handbrake alone.
items.altDiy: Timber wedges

items.name: Hardwood blocks
items.why: Between jack and subframe or crossbeam, and under a hub carrier.

items.name: Hydraulic workshop press
items.why: Front and rear bearings are press work. Jaguar seats front bearings with a 3 ton load.
items.altDiy: Take the vertical link or hub carrier to a machine shop with the new parts.

items.name: Metric socket set, 1/4 and 3/8 inch drive
items.why: Most fasteners on the car are metric.

items.name: 13 mm six-point socket
items.why: Sump drain plug.

items.name: 8 mm socket with extension
items.why: Thermostat housing front bolts and small trim fixings.

items.name: 8 mm hex bit socket
items.why: ZF plugs. On the X100 the 6HP26 fill plug sits in a tight spot.
items.altDiy: Hex socket with two adapters and a ratchet, or a ratcheting spanner on the hex. Jaguar uses adaptor 307-452.

items.name: Universal joint and short socket
items.why: Starter top bolt and the rear cam cover bolt.

items.name: Long socket extensions
items.why: Plugs, starter and cam cover work.

items.name: Ratchet with a stack of extensions
items.why: Reaches the diff fill plug from below.

items.name: 3/8 inch square drive bar
items.why: Fits the tensioner to swing it counter-clockwise.
items.altDiy: A torque wrench handle worked for JagRepair, though it is not ideal.

items.name: Wheel nut socket
items.why: Wheel nuts at 88-102 Nm. Socket size is not sourced, so measure yours first.

items.name: Low range torque wrench
items.why: Coils 5 Nm, MAF 2 Nm, bleed nipples, tensioner bolts.

items.name: Torque wrench, mid range
items.why: Plugs, drain plug, guide pins.

items.name: Torque wrench, large
items.size: to 200 Nm at least, and more for hub nuts
items.why: Wheel nuts, carrier bolts. Hub nuts need over 300 Nm.

items.name: Torque angle gauge
items.why: Water pump bolts and sprocket bolts are torque plus angle.
items.altDiy: Mark the socket and bolt with paint and judge 90 degrees by eye. Less accurate.

items.name: Thin open-ended spanners
items.why: Hold ball pin flats on anti-roll links so the boot does not twist.

items.name: Metric combination spanners
items.why: General use on exhaust and driveline.

items.name: Short 13 mm spanner
items.why: Starter top bolt.

items.name: Half-moon ring spanner
items.why: JTIS names this for cracking the top starter bolt.
items.altDiy: A short 13 mm spanner.

items.name: Bent 8 mm open spanner
items.why: The rear bolts of the 4.0 thermostat housing.
items.altDiy: Heat and bend a cheap 8 mm spanner close to the head. Make the bent section a little longer than you think.

items.name: 5/8 inch spanner
items.why: One owner used this on the fuel filter lines.

items.name: 3/4 inch spanner
items.why: One owner used this on the fuel filter.

items.name: Small ring spanner for bleed nipples
items.why: Nipples are low torque and round off easily.

items.name: Line spanners
items.why: Gearbox cooler pipes.

items.name: Torx T27
items.why: ZF pan bolts. Pan and filter screws on the 5HP24 are T27.

items.name: Torx T40
items.why: Forum reports of later pan bolts using this head.

items.name: Ball-end 10 mm hex
items.why: Cam sprocket bolt on the 4.0 at an angle past the front cover.
items.altDiy: Cut the L off a Craftsman ball-end hex key and drive it with a 10 mm socket, as Jensen did. A flat hex will not work here.

items.name: Flat screwdriver
items.why: Handbrake adjuster and general use.

items.name: Cross-head screwdriver
items.why: Radiator drain plug.
items.altDiy: A large washer turned the plug for one owner.

items.name: Long screwdriver
items.why: Inboard air box clips. Helps start the 4.0 thermostat rear bolts when the heads are slotted.

items.name: Screwdriver set
items.why: Door and trim screws.

items.name: Long-nose pliers
items.why: Wiggle a stuck coil boot off a plug.

items.name: Hose clip pliers
items.why: Coolant hose spring clips.
items.altDiy: Ordinary pliers, with patience.

items.name: Strap oil filter wrench
items.why: The filter is small, so the strap must close down far enough.

items.name: Spark plug socket
items.why: Reaches down the plug wells.
items.altDiy: A length of hose on the plug helps start the thread.

items.name: Piston retract tool
items.why: Pushes pistons back slowly.
items.altDiy: A G-clamp and an old pad.

items.name: Dial gauge with magnetic base
items.why: Disc run-out and rear hub end float. Jaguar lists JD 13A.

items.name: Vernier calipers
items.why: Measure the regulator stud before moving it.

items.name: Multimeter with a 10 A range
items.why: Parasitic drain and charging checks.

items.name: Smart battery charger
items.why: Forum users warn diagnostics need a strong charger. Start every electrical fault with a full battery.

items.name: Infrared thermometer
items.why: Reads gearbox pan temperature. One owner stopped at 47 C.
items.altDiy: A hand on the pan, but this is rough.

items.name: Hand fluid pump
items.why: ATF fill and diff oil. Cable-tie it to the car so you have both hands.

items.name: Large syringe
items.why: Fills the roof pump tank.

items.name: Funnel
items.why: Oil and coolant fill.

items.name: Measuring jug
items.why: Measure out what came out of the diff, then replace it.

items.name: Drain pan
items.why: Oil, coolant and ATF.

items.name: Brake bleed hose and bottle
items.why: Two per caliper on Brembo cars.
items.altDiy: Clear tube and a jam jar with fluid in the bottom.

items.name: Vacuum brush
items.why: Jaguar says to remove brake dust this way, never with an air line.

items.name: Wing covers
items.why: Jaguar uses paint protection covers on most jobs.
items.altDiy: Old blankets.

items.name: Plastic trim tools
items.why: Door casing studs and interior trim.

items.name: Plastic hook
items.why: Releases the stud on the door pocket trim.

items.name: Soft mallet
items.why: Release a stuck supercharger nose joint. Reported on a later engine.

items.name: Bench vice with soft jaws
items.why: Holds suspension parts. Jaguar fits jaw protectors.

items.name: Coil spring compressor
items.why: For stripping a front spring from its damper off the car.

items.name: Roof latch Allen key
items.why: Manual latch release in the header.

items.name: Blanking plugs
items.why: Close off hydraulic and cooler ports the moment they open.

items.name: Rotary tool with cut-off wheel
items.why: One owner cut the dipstick stud above the nut.

items.name: Threaded guide pins
items.why: Hold gaskets in place on refit. Reported on a later engine.
items.altDiy: Short lengths of threaded rod.

items.name: 1/2 inch square stock
items.why: Fits the diff fill plug so a ratchet can turn it from the side.

items.name: Axle thread protector
items.why: Saves the axle thread when pulling a rear hub.
items.altDiy: Fit the old nut flush on the shaft end.

items.name: Fuel line disconnect tool
items.why: Spring couplings. One owner reports buying one for about $5.

items.name: Paint marker
items.why: Marks pivot pins, propshaft flanges and hoses.

items.name: Stiff wire or ties
items.why: Hangs calipers. Jaguar forbids hanging them on the hose.

items.name: Strong wire
items.why: Ties the vertical link to the spring.

items.name: Linen tape
items.why: Holds the door glass up.

items.name: Soft toothbrush
items.why: Cleaning throttle body edges.

items.name: Clean lint-free rags
items.why: Block the openings at the front of the engine.

items.name: Absorbent cloths
items.why: Protect boot trim from hydraulic fluid.

items.name: A/C recovery and recharge service
items.why: Refrigerant must be recovered before A/C pipes open.
items.altDiy: Pay a mobile A/C service.

items.name: Rear spring compressors
items.why: Compress the rear spring on the car.
items.altDiy: A good pair of external coil clamps that seat fully on this spring. Inspect them before every use. A hire set is worth considering.

items.name: Spring retaining straps
items.why: Hold the upper mount to the spring.
items.altDiy: No sourced alternative. Do not improvise with tie straps.

items.name: Tie rod end taper separator
items.why: Tie rod ends only. It wrecks ball joint gaiters.
items.altDiy: A generic screw-type tie rod splitter of the same shape.

items.name: Ball joint taper separator
items.why: Upper ball joint.
items.altDiy: A generic ball joint splitter that avoids the gaiter.

items.name: Ball joint splitter
items.why: Lower ball joint.
items.altDiy: A generic splitter sized to avoid the gaiter.

items.name: Hub remover
items.why: Presses the front hub out.
items.altDiy: Machine shop.

items.name: Hub removal collets
items.why: Support the vertical link on the press.
items.altDiy: Machine shop.

items.name: Hub holding tool
items.why: Holds the hub by its studs for the very tight nuts.
items.altDiy: A steel bar drilled to the stud pattern.

items.name: Hub replacer
items.why: Fits the front hub.
items.altDiy: Machine shop.

items.name: Wheel bearing remover
items.why: Presses out the front bearing.
items.altDiy: A press mandrel of the right size.

items.name: Wheel bearing replacer
items.why: Fits the front bearing by its outer race.
items.altDiy: A press mandrel that bears only on the outer race.

items.name: ABS rotor nut socket
items.why: Fits the castellated front rotor nut.
items.altDiy: No sourced alternative. Machine shops may have one.

items.name: Circlip pliers
items.why: Tips must not protrude past the ears, or the seal is hurt.
items.altDiy: Good internal circlip pliers with short tips.

items.name: Rear hub puller
items.why: Pulls the hub off the axle shaft splines.
items.altDiy: A heavy stud-mounted hub puller.

items.name: Rear hub remover
items.why: Two-piece press tool with a recess for the handbrake cable housing.
items.altDiy: Machine shop.

items.name: Bearing cup replacer adaptors
items.why: Fit the inner and outer rear cups.
items.altDiy: A bearing race driver set.

items.name: Driver handle
items.why: Used with the cup adaptors.
items.altDiy: Handle from a race driver set.

items.name: Rear hub spacer replacer
items.why: Used when measuring rear end float.
items.altDiy: Machine shop.

items.name: Oil seal remover and replacer
items.why: Seats the rear hub seals.
items.altDiy: A flat driver of the right diameter.

items.name: Engine support beam
items.why: Holds the engine from the wing channels while the crossbeam is lowered.
items.altDiy: A hired engine support bar, protected at the wing channels.

items.name: Camshaft setting tool
items.why: Locks the cams during sprocket bolt work.
items.altDiy: Laser 5147 includes a pair of bridges. Jensen bought one and did one bank at a time. Method B avoids it altogether.

items.name: Timing chain tensioning tool
items.why: Counters the sprocket and tensions the chain. Square hole takes a 1/2 inch bar.
items.altDiy: Laser 5147 kit, or the home-made versions Jensen read about. Laser says not to load its version against sprocket bolts.

items.name: Crankshaft setting peg
items.why: Fits the crank sensor hole to set the crank on 2003-on 4.2 cars. Never use it to hold the pulley bolt.
items.altDiy: Laser 5147 pin combines the 303-645 and 303-531 designs.

items.name: Crankshaft pulley remover
items.why: The pulley is very tight.
items.altDiy: Laser 5147 includes a puller.

items.name: Crankshaft pulley locking tool
items.why: Holds the pulley for the 375 Nm bolt.
items.altDiy: A strap or pulley holding tool rated for the torque.

items.name: 12 mm Ribe bit socket
items.why: 4.2 exhaust sprocket bolt.
items.altDiy: A 12 mm Ribe bit from a bit set.

items.name: Belt tensioner release tool
items.why: Unloads the supercharger belt tensioner.
items.altDiy: A slim bar that fits the tensioner.

items.name: Fuel pressure gauge
items.why: Screws on the rail valve to release pressure.
items.altDiy: Press the Schrader valve into a rag, or pull the pump fuse at idle.

items.name: Fill plug adaptor
items.why: 6HP26 fill plug.
items.altDiy: 8 mm hex and adapters. See socket-8mm-hex.

items.name: Generic OBD-II reader or ELM327 adapter
items.why: Reads engine P codes, live data and fuel trims. Fine for a misfire or lean code. Owners report it does not reach Jaguar transmission or ABS codes. An ELM327 with the Torque app was reported on a 2005 XK8 and XJ8 for basic reading only. A cheap adapter may also fail outright.
items.altDiy: Good first purchase.

items.name: Multi-system handheld scanner
items.why: Coverage is unpredictable. On one XJS an Autel read transmission and ABS but not engine. Check the maker's coverage list for your VIN before buying. This item was not verified on an X100.

items.name: Jaguar WDS, IDS or SDD
items.why: The dealer route. Jaguar's gearbox level check calls for an approved diagnostic system to read fluid temperature, and owners say ABS and airbag fault finding needs it. Slow to load, and needs a strong battery charger on the car. Some versions want an internet connection. Wrong programming can brick modules. The cost shown is the roughly £100 an owner reported for a clone lead and software bundle, not a genuine system.
items.altDiy: A specialist with the kit charges by the session. Owners also buy a clone lead and software bundle.

items.name: Mongoose-type J2534 lead
items.why: Owners commonly use a Mongoose Pro lead with SDD or IDS. The licensing position of clone leads was not confirmed.
items.altDiy: Clone lead, with the risks above.
Laser 5147 pin combines the 303-645 and 303-531 designs.
items.name: Crankshaft setting peg, 4.0
items.why: Seats in the timing slot of the drive plate through the crank sensor hole on 4.0 cars.

items.name: Front coil spring compressor
items.why: Holds the front spring and damper assembly so the damper nut can come off. The spring is under extreme tension.

items.name: Belt tensioner spanner
items.why: Turns the 1997-2002 tensioner idler assembly by its left-hand centre bolt to release the belt.

items.altDiy: Jaguar allows another suitable type.
items.name: Fuel injection pressure test equipment
items.why: Releases fuel pressure at the valve on the cross-over pipe on 1997-2002 cars.

items.name: Hand fuel suction pump
items.why: Drains the tank before a 1997-2002 fuel filter change. Jaguar says manually operated only.

items.name: DC clamp meter
items.why: Reads battery drain and individual junction box leads without breaking the circuit, which is what Jaguar prefers.

items.name: Service dipstick, W5A580
items.why: The supercharged 4.0 box has a sealed tube. This dipstick reads the level against 25 C and 80 C marks.

items.altDiy: A strap wrench that closes down far enough, though it cannot be torqued.
items.name: Oil filter wrench
items.why: Lets the oil filter be torqued to 18 Nm, the fix for filters loosening in service.

items.name: Jump leads
items.why: Heavy enough to carry the starter current. The handbook asks for high quality leads.

gaps: costGbp is null for almost every tool. UK prices could not be sourced because the search budget ran out. Laser Tools' page gave no price. Jensen's 2006 US prices ($125 cam lock, $75 tension tool, $50 crank tool) were not converted. The only GBP figure is about £100 for a clone diagnostic bundle, reported by an owner.

altDiy text for hub, bearing and press tools is practical advice from this project, not a sourced method. Sourced alternatives are the Laser 5147 kit, Jensen's cut hex key, the bent 8 mm spanner, the cable-tie method, and owner workarounds for the fill plug and diff plug.
Jaguar tool numbers are from the 2003 to 2006 manual, JTIS and Laser's sheet. Laser lists the kit for X100 1996 to 2006.

OBD coverage: no head-to-head test of readers on an X100 was found. The clearest reader statement comes from an XJS thread. ELM327 on a 2005 XK8 was reported for basic reading only. Whether early UK 4.0 cars answer generic OBD-II was not confirmed. Coverage of Autel, iCarsoft, Foxwell and similar units was not verified. WDS and IDS use on X100 is confirmed by a JLR bulletin on legacy models and by owners, but licensing of clone software was not confirmed.
Sizes marked null were not sourced. Torque wrench ranges are this project's practical suggestions.
